scope: Historical browser-WASM observations only. These runs do not validate the final threaded default, native runtime, physical hardware or the unavailable uploaded user application.

validation.browser: actual isolated static exports and same-guest serial/frame/controller observations

evidence_integrity.original_reference_firmware_file_rehash: PASS; full 16 MiB image matches its browser receipt and original profile hash.

interpretation: Baseline reference: DOM requests near 100/300/800ms and raw 300ms were accepted, with actual SCS present positions changing, but its original M5.Touch API reported no paired screen events. The raw-input failure weakens a moving-geometry-only explanation.

Constructor A/B: screen press/release works before and after the original StackChan(i2c=1,uart=1) constructor in a main-only derivative of the same reference base. No new I2C object or pin/frequency replacement was introduced by the diagnostic before construction. This weakens a permanently disabled FT path or constructor-caused persistent bus break; it does not exclude all I2C races.

The stock MicroPython wrapper does not expose M5.Touch.isEnabled. Its absence is not evidence that touch is disabled. After construction, independent guest I2C FT reads observed both count=1 and count=0.

Timing-only derivative keeps the original UART, Si12T, drawing and sleep workload. The telemetry strip dominates foreground work; roughly 1.64-1.75 seconds between input polling passes can entirely cover an 800ms contact. The measurements include instrumentation overhead and are not the exact original image.

Baseline Arduino instrumentation also caused long foreground redraw and synchronous angle-read work. Paired screen releases arrived roughly 4.4-4.8 seconds late; these failures are retained as observation-gate failures rather than proof of permanently swallowed releases.

Minimal foreground optimization is insufficient: its true 103.27ms DOM hold is still missed. DOM 300/800ms touch and motion overlap pass. Raw 300ms touch/coordinates pass but only one QOM sample is inside the hold, so motion-overlap remains an evidence gap.

Intentional blocked controls omit M5.update while the independent original BSP Motion task runs. A short application-level miss inside that interval is an expected negative control, not evidence of electrical exclusion between servo and touch.

timing_observation.boundary: API timings show no observed 250ms timeout. This does not prove a physical timing limit or matching-ELF function equivalence.
